There are electric bikes, there are electric motorcycles, and then there are machines like the Aniioki A9 Pro Max that plant a flag somewhere in the increasingly large no-man’s-land between the two.
Technically, it has pedals. You can pedal it fairly effectively too, with the actually adjustable seat. You can even pedal it for fun, which is more than I can say for some of the increasingly motorcycle-shaped “e-bikes” I’ve tested lately.
But let’s get something out of the way right at the beginning: this isn’t a street-legal electric bicycle in the US . Not when we’re talking about dual motors producing up to 6,000W of peak power and speeds of around 45 mph.
And you know what? That’s fine. As long as we’re all honest about what this thing is.

A whole lot of bike
The Aniioki A9 Pro Max is absolutely massive, and the spec sheet makes that abundantly clear.
The version I tested uses a pair of 2,500W direct-drive hub motors, one in each wheel, with Aniioki claiming 3,000W peak power from each motor. That gives the bike a combined peak figure of 6,000W and up to 250 Nm of combined torque. It’s hard to overstate how massive that is.
Then there’s the battery. You can choose between a 60V 70Ah pack with 4.2 kWh of capacity or an even larger 60V 80Ah pack packing 4.8 kWh. For comparison, many typical commuter e-bikes have somewhere around 500-700 Wh of battery. The smaller battery here is roughly six to eight times that size. That’s absolutely in the territory of legit light electric motorcycles.
Aniioki claims up to 230+ miles (370 km) of pedal-assist range, though as usual, you should take maximum e-bike range figures as best-case numbers. Using the throttle and enjoying those big motors is going to dramatically reduce that figure. Even so, with more than 4 kWh of battery underneath you, range anxiety isn’t exactly the first thing that comes to mind.
All that hardware comes with a predictable penalty: weight. The 70Ah model tips the scales at around 188 lb (85 kg), while the 80Ah version approaches 193 lb (87.5 kg). Those aren’t e-bike weights. Those are motorcycle weights. Again, you can see the direction this is going.
But surprisingly, you can actually pedal it
Here’s where the A9 Pro Max gets more interesting to me.
A lot of high-powered e-motos include pedals seemingly as a regulatory fig leaf. They’re technically there, but the geometry is so bad that nobody in their right mind would want to pedal the thing farther than across a parking lot. Even some smaller and presumably Class 2 legal e-bikes that have moto-style frames are nearly unpedalable for actual riding over any reasonable distance.
But the A9 here is actually pedalable thanks to having something that more closely resembles a bicycle seat, plus adjustability that lets riders dial in the correct seat height.
The A9 Pro Max feels more like a strange combination of an oversized fat-tire e-bike and a small electric motorcycle. There’s a Shimano 7-speed drivetrain and a huge 72-tooth chainring, meaning the pedals aren’t entirely ornamental.
I actually enjoyed pedaling it with the pedal assist engaged. You’re obviously not going to mistake a nearly 200-pound machine rolling on enormous 26 x 4.8-inch tires for a lightweight fitness bike, but there’s something fun about contributing some human power while two giant hub motors do most of the heavy lifting.
And when you don’t feel like pedaling, there’s a full-twist throttle waiting for you.
That combination is really the appeal here. You can ride it more like an e-bike when the mood strikes, or twist the throttle and treat it more like a lightweight e-moto.
And again, I don’t want to beat a dead horse here, but remember: the pedals don’t make this an electric bicycle. It’s still an e-moto, but it’s one that you can actually have fun pedaling. You can treat it like a mech suit, where pedaling translates into crazy power, as if you have super-human legs. And with the insanely large 72t chainring, pedaling at higher speeds is actually doable. Though I’ll tell you right now, pedaling at 40 mph (64 km/h) is not exactly a normal or natural feeling.
And it’s worth pointing out that at a starting price of US $2,899 (or more for the larger battery capacities), that’s a fairly reasonable price compared to most e-motos that can be more limiting in how and where you can ride them.
Motorcycle performance deserves motorcycle hardware
Fortunately, Aniioki seems to understand that putting this much power on two wheels requires more serious components than the average bicycle.
The braking setup is particularly wild. There are two massive 300mm brake rotors on the front wheel and another 300mm rotor out back, along with a linked CBS braking system. The front uses custom eight-piston calipers (the pair of quad-piston calipers) while the rear gets a custom six-piston setup.
There’s also an adjustable air-suspension fork with 110mm of travel, rear suspension to smooth out bumps at higher speeds, integrated lighting and turn signals, and a large five-inch display that even incorporates features like Bluetooth audio and a recording camera.
Know where you can ride it
That brings us to the elephant in the room.
In the US, consumer-product rules generally define a low-speed electric bicycle around a motor of less than 750W and a maximum motor-powered speed below 20 mph (32 km/h), while individual states use their own operating laws that typically match the familiar Class 1/2/3 framework. A 6,000W machine capable of around 45 mph (72 km/h) blows straight through normal limits.
So please don’t see pedals and assume this belongs on your local bicycle path.
Where and how you can legally operate something like the A9 Pro Max depends on your local laws and whether it can qualify under another vehicle category. For many owners, the sensible place to enjoy its full performance is going to be private property or other areas where such vehicles are permitted.
That caveat doesn’t make the bike itself bad. It just means buyers need to understand what they’re buying.
And judged on what it actually is rather than what the word “e-bike” on the product page suggests, I had a lot of fun on it.
There are certainly riders who would look at a nearly 200-pound, 45 mph machine and say, “Why not just buy an electric motorcycle?” That’s a perfectly reasonable question.
But I also understand the appeal of this weird middle ground. The A9 Pro Max retains enough bicycle DNA that you can pedal it around and enjoy pedal assist, yet has enough battery and motor underneath you to deliver something much closer to small-motorcycle performance when you twist the throttle.
Imagine going off-road and getting to fly up hills while pedaling hard, but then being able to switch to throttle once your legs get worn out. Sure, it’s not everyone’s cup of tea, but it’s a cup of tea.
This bike is big. It’s heavy. It’s absurdly powerful by e-bike standards. And it absolutely isn’t the machine I’d recommend for someone looking for a normal street-legal electric bicycle.
But if what you actually want is a big, powerful electric two-wheeler that still lets you turn the pedals when the mood strikes, the Aniioki A9 Pro Max makes a surprisingly compelling argument for this increasingly bizarre category of pedal-equipped e-motos.

Mercedes Is Taking Its Obsession With Screens to a Whole New Level
25 photos
Photo: Mercedes-Benz
Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in. Am I right? Just when it seemed carmakers were finally coming around to the idea that not every function needs a display, Mercedes went and did the old "hold my beer" routine. The Stuttgart-based carmaker is busy at work exploring entirely new places to put displays in. For the sake of safety and communication, of course.
The first bit of tech they decided to showcase is the intelligent display, which is meant to enable a new form of communication between the vehicle and its surroundings. They managed to integrate LED display elements directly into the windows - like the back windows or the rear window - so that they could project warning signs, safety symbols, and other traffic-related information.
When no content is displayed, the LED elements laminated into the glass remain basically invisible.
Regarding the rear window, the carmaker could use mini LEDs to show brake lights and various warning symbols, whereas micro LEDs could offer higher resolution and display more complex animations (like you see in the image above).
Then there's the holographic display, where the windshield itself can become an on-demand communication surface. It's basically another head-up display, only this time on the passenger side - except that unlike the driver's head-up display, this one is a lot more complex. The best part is that it's only visible from specific angles, so the driver can't see what's being shown on the passenger side (and vice versa).
This could be used for navigation, video calls, various driving information and even entertainment purposes.
"The future of mobility is not created through promises, but through precision and proven engineering excellence. With innovations that offer clear benefits in our customers' everyday lives, we are shaping the mobility of tomorrow - continuously, consistently and with a clear focus on the future," said Mercedes VP of development innovations, operations & digitalization, Ida Wolf.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz That's not the only new technology Mercedes would like us to know about - meet the Mercedes-Benz Power Converter. A piece of tech that uses programmable micro-converters to control the energy flows of individual battery cells, thus providing a constant high-voltage output of up to 800 volts at all times.
This system could enable Mercedes to design more versatile hardware units in terms of batteries and powertrains. It could also improve range and efficiency for both electric vehicles as well as plug-in hybrids.
As far as I'm concerned, full speed ahead on that latter tech. As for the new display tech, whatever doesn't bother the driver visually is OK in my book. I'm just not sure about the rear passenger window displays. They could become a distraction for other drivers in various conditions. But there's no need to worry about this type of stuff ahead of time.

New Zealand’s Foodstuffs North Island Limited has given its latest electric semi truck an electrifying new identity, courtesy of a second-grade student at a local elementary school.
The Chinese-built DeepWay Star began delivering chilled and frozen groceries across New Zealand’s lower North Island earlier this year – and, after a naming competition organized with students at Russell Street School in Palmerston North, the big HD EV has got a new name: Evie .
The winning name came from Year 2 (read: second grade) student named Madison, who beat out suggestions including Buzzy Bee, Lightning, and Bolt. Madison got to officially unveil the truck’s new name alongside her classmates, local officials and Foodstuffs representatives.
“Our trucks are out on the road every day delivering food to stores and communities, so we thought it would be great to get the kids involved and give our first electric truck a bit of personality,” explains Foodstuffs North Island General Manager Supply Chain, Yang Zhang. “There were some brilliant ideas, but Evie was a pretty fitting name for an EV. The best part is knowing Madison and the other students will be able to spot Evie out on the road and know they played a part in it.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Looking forward
Madison was allowed to do the unveiling honors, revealing Evie’s new name alongside her other classmates, Palmerston North’s Mayor, Grant Smith, local MP Tangi Utikeri, and local PAK’nSAVE, New World, and Four Square grocers who will be receiving deliveries from Evie.
In its first few months on the road, Evie’s travelled nearly 45,000 kilometers (~28,000 miles) and avoided more than 81,000 kg of harmful carbon emissions – which the company claims is roughly equivalent to taking 35 ICE cars off the road for a full year .
As for the truck itself, it has a sort of Tesla-ish, anteater-y look, and significantly longer range than the StarWay, offering more than 500 km (~310 miles) of range from its 600 kWh CATL-built LFP battery packs that can plug into charge ports two at a time for lickety-quick charging in about 30 minutes . If that’s too long of a wait, the Star can swap its tired batteries for fresh ones in special battery-sway stations in just six minutes .
The DeepWay’s electric motors put out 491 kW (~660 hp) of power, and a positively tectonic 75,000 (!) Nm (~55,000 lb-ft) (!!) of torque – more than enough to get the 50 tons (100,000 lb.) of GVWR it’s rated for up to speed.

Photo: Port of Long Beach
By Gavin van Marle
5 November 2026
The Californian port of Long Beach is predicted to handle more than 10m teu this year, for the first time.
“It’s been a peak year,” Port of Long Beach CEO Noel Hacegaba told The Loadstar on the sidelines of the World Ports Conference in London this week.
“This could well be the first 10m teu year for us.”
His comments followed a record-breaking September, when throughput hit 997,177 teu, its busiest month ever, surpassing the previous record set in October 2024.
In the first nine months of the year, Long Beach has moved just under 7.8m, up 3.9% compared with the same period last year.
Dr Hacegaba said the very strong growth in transpacific volumes had been due to a combination of shippers front-loading imports to avoid the threatened USTR 301 port fees on Chinese-owned and -operated vessels, concerns about the viability of the Panama Canal as El Nino emerged, and fuel costs.
“There’s no question a lot of front-loading has been going on, and the recent decision to postpone these [port] fees has moved the goalposts – and we now expect another round of front-loading before the new 9 January deadline.
“Then you have worries about the Panama Canal, which has seen cargo diverted to the US west coast, and that’s coming on top of shipping lines increasing fuel costs,” he said.
The cargo surge had led to MSC deploying some of its largest ships, of 24,000 teu capacity, on its standalone transpacific Sentosa service, which calls at Long Beach’s Total Terminal International (TTI) facility
“Normally the ships on this service are smaller, but we have handled some of their largest ships, with 100% discharging and 100% loading – this is a glimpse of our future,” Dr Hacegaba said.
According to Xeneta’s eeSea liner database, the usual average capacity of a Sentosa service vessel is 18,500 teu, with its largest at 19,500 teu. However, during the peak demand period of August, September, October, the carrier deployed two 24,000 teu vessels on the string, MSC Nela and MSC Arina .
“It’s also notable that 50% of TTI’s inbound boxes leave the port by train,” he added.
On the threat of industrial action at Long Beach and neighbouring Los Angeles, Dr Hacegaba said: “We are closely monitoring the negotiations between ILWU Local 26 and the Pacific Maritime Association, and we remain hopeful both sides will reach an agreement soon.
“While the affected watchmen provide security within individual terminals, port-wide security provided by the Harbor Patrol and the Long Beach Police Department continues uninterrupted during negotiations.
“Although Port of Long Beach is not a party to the negotiations, we want to assure our customers that we remain committed to moving cargo through our port safely and reliably,” he said.
Meanwhile, the forthcoming closure of the Vincent Thomas Bridge in the San Pedro area for refurbishment works – due 7 November and lasting for 16 months – is forecast to disrupt hinterland cargo movements, and has led the port and its terminal operators to offer hauliers additional gate hour openings on Friday evenings and Saturdays for a six-week period.
It’s part of a pilot programme “that could be extended and is among the numerous measures Long Beach and its partners have developed to reduce the impacts of the bridge closure on people and cargo”, explained Dr Hacegaba.

Photo: kolesa.ru
Bentley , the iconic ultra-luxury British automaker from Crewe, England, has recently led the automotive news world’s headlines as it ramped up interest for the latest model release: their first-ever, all-electric, series-production model, the all-new Torcal crossover SUV.
Thanks to this brand-new release, the company now bests its former family member turned archenemy, Rolls-Royce, because it has two crossover SUVs, the new Bentley Torcal and the ‘classic’ Bentley Bentayga with ICE power under the hood. There are also the hybrid Continental GT grand tourer along with its Flying Spur sedan sibling, offering a balanced model range.
That’s not all, of course, as the brand also revealed recently a reinvention of the Bentley showroom recently, kicking off with the oldest Bentley retailer: Jack Barclay in London. Established in 1927, almost a century ago, it was named after a racing driver of that era and is currently operated by H.R. Owen.
The company also has a fresh business strategy, according to the rumor mill, with the all-new Bentley Torcal headlining a business plan that aims to keep both ICE and hybrid models alongside slowed all-electric investments, so a new EV model isn’t coming before the turn of the decade. Instead, gasoline options are here to stay, mostly electrified to make them both more potent and efficient.
Of course, the rumor mill continues to pay special attention to the future of the Volkswagen AG brand, and just recently the good folks at Kolesa, along with their resident pixel master Nikita Chuicko, aka ' kelsonik ' on social media, imagined the next-gen Bentley sedan, the Flying Spur, going through a comprehensive CGI morphing.
The Bentley Flying Spur would potentially get fresh styling elements adapted from the Torcal while retaining the classic profile to make sure it doesn’t alienate faithful customers – and it could simply continue with the current hybrid V8 powertrain options. Of course, that’s not all – because now the news outlet , along with their resident pixel master, has also envisioned the potential look of a refreshed fourth-gen Bentley Continental GT or even a complete remastering for a new iteration.
In their unofficial, hypothetical design project, the massive grand tourer would be slightly different from the Torcal-inspired Flying Spur – it could have the new vertical front fascia with the fresh grille, but the GT would return to the double circular headlights as per the first three generations, with the new cluster sporting halo ring lights as daytime running LEDs.
The rear, meanwhile, could adopt a more direct link to the new Torcal, featuring the same LED taillights and the fender separation. Under the hood, Bentley wouldn’t have to change much – perhaps just offer more power for the Ultra Performance Hybrid and Performance Hybrid systems, which currently have combined ratings of 671 and 771 horsepower.

By Alex Lennane
5 November 2026
Uncollected imports are clogging cargo warehouses at Taiwan Taoyuan Airport, tying up dollies and slowing aircraft unloading as equipment arrives to support the island’s AI and semiconductor industries, according to local forwarders.
Seko Logistics has reported handling pressure affecting China Airlines, EVA Air, and Starlux, alongside selected China Airlines flight cancellations, including US-bound freighter services.
“Reminds me of Covid days,” one forwarder told The Loadsta r.
“There is a shortage of dollies at the airport, so cargo cannot be unloaded from aircraft and towed to the ground handlers for breakdown, etc.”
The source said the equipment shortage stemmed from freight accumulating in warehouses because consignees had yet to collect it.
“There is so much freight sitting in the GHA warehouse and this not being collected by customers. There apparently is cargo from early September still sitting there.”
The reason for the delayed collections remains uncertain, but the source suggested incoming equipment was reaching Taiwan before facilities intended to receive it were ready.
“We are not 100% sure why customers are not collecting the freight, but we understand this also stems from the customers’ manufacturing facilities not being ready to take on this equipment yet. So, the whole supply chain is backlogged.”
That accumulation was creating a knock-on shortage of equipment needed to move newly arrived cargo.
“Because the GHA is so full, no new cargo can be brought in, so all the freight is sitting outside the warehouse on the dollies, resulting in a dolly shortage,” the forwarder explained.
“Apparently, it is primarily the China Airlines (CI) warehouse that is full, so CI services are most affected.”
The congestion was also spreading beyond the immediately affected warehouse, the source added.
“Now the bridge connecting the main terminal to the GHA is packed with these loaded dollies so it’s blocking the way, and other GHA cargo also being slowed down and affected.”
The forwarder attributed the pressure to equipment imports supporting Taiwan’s technology sector.
“All this arising from the incredible imports Taiwan is now facing for AI, semi-con and AI-related services. Manufacturing fully ramped up with so much new equipment coming in to support it is choking everything.”

Seko warned of potential delays in cargo breakdown and build-up, longer export processing times and changes to shipment departure schedules. It also reported receiving notifications of selected China Airlines cancellations, including US-bound freighters, but did not identify the flights or establish whether the cancellations resulted from the handling congestion.
Rotate data shows inbound widebody freighter capacity to Taiwan increased 20% in the week from 29 October to 4 November compared with the preceding seven days.
Narita-Taipei capacity increased by about 1,000 tonnes, or 49%, while Shanghai Pudong added 595 tonnes, up 76%, and Hong Kong added 572 tonnes, up 20%. Los Angeles-Taipei capacity rose 66%, adding 519 tonnes.
The increase followed a 15% decline in the previous week, however, indicating a rebound.
Outbound Taiwan-US widebody freighter capacity also increased, rising 4% over the same weekly comparison. Within that total, China Airlines’ capacity fell 8%, or 263 tonnes, while EVA, UPS, and Atlas recorded increases.
The figures suggest the reported handling disruption is occurring alongside growth in overall US-bound lift, rather than a general contraction in capacity.

Credit: AF-KLM
By Alex Lennane
5 November 2026
KLM plans to consolidate cargo handling at Schiphol to accommodate additional freight without hiring more staff, as AI supply chains and disruption to ocean shipping strengthen parent Air France-KLM’s cargo business.
The changes form part of a wider restructuring, announced today, aimed at improving KLM’s finances and its ability to fund investment.
Freight carried on passenger aircraft and freighters will be handled in KLM’s own warehouse at Schiphol, said the airline, adding that the consolidation would help attract more transfer freight and prepare for a new cargo terminal, scheduled for completion in 2035.
“The increased cargo volumes will ultimately be handled without hiring additional employees,” KLM said.
It plans to achieve this through “simpler processes, greater automation and deploying employees across different activities”. It also intends to expand services for customers requiring additional support, although it gave no further detail.
The announcement follows conversations at last week’s TIACA Air Cargo Forum in Miami, where The Loadstar heard that AI infrastructure shipments were contributing to transit cargo flows through Amsterdam.
Air France-KLM’s third-quarter results provided evidence of the wider demand trend. Group cargo revenue increased 25.2% year on year, to €677m ($760m), while cargo traffic revenue rose 24.9%, to €566m.
The group attributed the growth to sea-to-air modal shift amid disruption around the Suez Canal and Strait of Hormuz, alongside AI-related demand.
“The surge in air freight demand driven by AI-related supply chains tightened global market conditions,” it said.
This helped the group win additional volumes and full-freighter charter business, supporting yields.
KLM’s cargo traffic, measured in revenue tonne-km, rose 15.7% against capacity growth of 4.5%. Its cargo load factor increased 5.2 percentage points, to 53.9%.
Across Air France-KLM, tonnage rose 5%, to 236,000 tonnes. Revenue per available tonne-km increased 21.9% at constant currency, with demand outpacing capacity growth. Scheduled and unscheduled maintenance constrained freighter availability.
Schiphol’s latest monthly figures show September cargo volumes of 127,750 tonnes, up 8% year on year, with growth of 10% over the first nine months. Freighters accounted for 54% of September tonnage, and belly cargo 46%.
Despite cargo’s performance, KLM said its overall profitability remained insufficient to support investment. Third-quarter adjusted operating profit rose to €458m, from a restated €352m a year earlier.
“Fuel prices continue to put pressure on our results, our cost base remains too high,” said KLM CEO Marjan Rintel.
The Dutch carrier is seeking a further €1bn improvement in annual earnings, taking its total target to €1.4bn, and at least an 8% structural productivity increase by 2028.
The wider programme involves around 5,000 positions whose work has been, or will be, reorganised, including transfers to external providers and the parent group. Productivity improvements are expected to result in approximately 1,000 fewer positions at KLM.
The airline expects to limit the impact through natural attrition, voluntary arrangements, and internal transfers.

By Alexander Whiteman
5 November 2026
Maersk experienced a 27% year-on-year bump in its third-quarter revenues, hitting $18.1bn, buoyed by a sharp rise in container freight rates that more than offset a slight dip in volumes, prompting it to join ONE in revising its full-year outlook.
While the Danish shipping and logistics group said revenue growth had been driven by all its divisions, Ocean Services accounted for the largest contribution, some $12.6bn, an increase of 37% on the same period last year.
Group CEO Vincent Clerc said: “We delivered a strong quarter across our businesses. Despite continued geopolitical uncertainty and disruptions, global trade has remained remarkably resilient.”
Average loaded freight rates increased 46% year on year, to $3,287 per 40ft, with Mr Clerc singling out investment in electrification, energy, and AI infrastructure as one of the core drivers of growth.
The rate increase offset moderate volume declines, added the company, down 0.8% over the three-month period to 3.37m feu, which Maersk attributed to the severe weather in Asia and the Strait of Hormuz, although volumes were, nevertheless, 0.3% up on the second quarter.
The carrier noted that global container demand had grown between 2% and 4%, year on year, during the quarter, with resilient trade flows supported by consumer spending and investment.
Double-digit revenue growth was also forthcoming for Logistics & Services, which recorded a 13% upturn in turnover, to $4.5bn, from $4bn a year earlier, while Forwarding saw solid growth in airfreight and project logistics.
Pulling in 2.6% more volume, Terminals generated revenue of $1.5bn, up 4.9% from $1.4bn a year earlier – with Africa and Europe faring well – which the company said was driven by improved rates, higher storage revenue, and a favourable cargo mix.
Across the group, EBITDA increased 75%, to $4.7bn, from $2.7bn, with EBIT up from $1.3bn a year earlier to $3.3bn, with Ocean again leading this, reporting a massive EBIT spike, from $567m in 2025 to $2.6bn this year.
This strong quarterly performance, as well as expecting an overall 4% volume rise for the year, Maersk upped its full-year earnings guidance for the third time, for EBITDA from $10.5bn-$12.5bn to $14bn-$14.5bn, and raised EBIT expectation from $4.5bn-$6.5bn to $8bn-$8.5bn.

They Bought a Lexus LC for $123,494, Put It Up for Sale Immediately, Refused $163,500
15 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Yeah, it’s not a clickbait story, as this actually happened, and if you are curious whether the Lexus LC in question is still for sale, then the answer is yes, and it’s a brand new car.
The seller reportedly bought it new in September 2026 and refrained from driving it. Therefore, this machine has only 20 miles (30 km) on the clock. The selling price was $123,494, as per the window stick attached in the gallery, and the owner believes that the vehicle is worth more than $163,500. That’s because he refused to sell it for the latter sum at an online auction that recently ended.
This 2026 Lexus LC 500 Inspiration Series Coupe was advertised on Cars&Bids. The gavel hit the table on November 4, 2026, and the premium grand tourer failed to change hands, even if it would have made its owner a nice profit of $40,000. The model is worth between $140,000 and over $175,000 in today’s market, and it’s up for you to decide whether the seller is being greedy or if they might make even more money from parting ways with their brand new LC.
The car is finished in Smoke Matte Gray and has a white and black cockpit. It rides on 21-inch forged wheels, has active rear-wheel steering, a limited-slip differential, and a carbon fiber roof. Additional features mentioned in the ad include the head-up display, leather upholstery, heated and ventilated seats at the front, a Mark Levinson premium sound system, and the Lexus Safety System+ 2.5 bundle of driving assistance gizmos.
Photo: Cars&Bids Power is supplied by a V8 engine, and it is a naturally aspirated 5.0-liter unit, in case you forgot. The Lexus LC 500 had 471 horsepower in this configuration, which translates to 477 metric horsepower and 351 kilowatts, and 398 lb-ft (540 Nm) of torque. A ten-speed automatic transmission deploys everything to the rear axle.
Mind you, this model is not exactly a dragster disguised as a comfortable and very good-looking premium grand tourer, but it won’t make a fool of itself either in a straight-line acceleration. That’s because it needs 4.4 seconds to zip from 0-60 mph (0-97 kph). The convertible is two-tenths of a second slower. And the standing quarter mile takes over 13 seconds, with an exit speed of 110 mph (175 kph).
This paragraph would normally be dedicated to the known flaws, but since the 2026 Lexus LC 500 Inspiration Series Coupe in question has only 20 miles under its belt, it is a brand new vehicle with no issues. It has a clean Carfax history report, a clean Virginia title, and is located in Centreville, VA. By the way, due to the fact that it is new, it hasn’t required any servicing yet. And there are no modifications on deck, not even tinted windows, or a paint protection film.
In addition to the car, the next owner will get two key fobs, one wallet key, the owner’s manuals, and the window sticker. Thus, if you want one of these in your life and are willing to get it at a very steep premium compared to what it initially cost, then you should get in touch with the seller and make an offer. But whatever you do, you should know that they likely won’t accept anything under $163,500.
Photo: Cars&Bids We’d want to know how much the seller hopes to get from parting ways with their new Lexus LC 500 Inspiration Series Coupe from the 2026 model year, but your guess is as good as ours. And to be honest, we would not be surprised to learn that they might try to get very close to the $200,000 mark. After all, that’s what some dealers are doing.
Now, if you were really shopping for a fresh Lexus LC 500 in the Inspiration Series configuration with a fixed-roof design and the model sat at the very top of your shopping list, would you really try to get this example knowing that its first and only owner refused to let it go for $163,500? If you said yes, then you may want to reach out to them here on Cars&Bids and discuss the details. And if you end up buying it, then feel free to tell us what you paid for it.
In the meantime, we will remind you that Lexus pulled the plug on the LC a few months ago. Production of this model ended in August 2026, as that is when the final copy rolled off the assembly line at the Motomachi (Toyota City) factory in Japan, a little over 9 years after it entered production.
The LC was based on the TNGA-L platform, shared with the Lexus LS, the Toyota Crown Sedan, and the Mirai, and was offered as a two-door coupe and a two-door convertible. Besides the V8 engine, customers could also get it with a hybridized gasoline engine. The electrified 3.5L V6 made 354 hp and 350 lb-ft (475 Nm) of torque, enabling 0-60 mph in 4.7 seconds.

2027 Triumph TF 450-X Gets Upgrades to Survive MXGP Racing Next Year
21 photos
Photo: Triumph
In the fall of 2025, British bike maker Triumph stormed the world of off-road 450cc class motorcycles with the new TF 450-X. Building on the TF 450-RC introduced a year prior, it rapidly went on to race in the AMA Supercross and Pro Motocross as part of the Triumph Factory Racing team. As it is gearing up to race in the FIM MXGP Motocross World Championship as well next year, the bike got a pretty comprehensive overhaul.
To get it ready for the rigors of the new series it enters, the off-roader got to keep its most important components, including the aluminum spine frame with a hydroformed swingarm and the 450cc four-stroke single-cylinder engine sitting inside it.
Power levels remain the same as before, meaning 62 horsepower at 9,500 rpm and 50 Nm of torque at 7,000 rpm, which, for a machine that tips the scales at just 238 pounds (108 kg), is more than enough. The troop is controlled by means of a five-speed transmission, with Brembo hardware taking care of stopping power.
Triumph talks of revised engine calibration, an updated cylinder head, and a new clutch pack for the 2027 version of the motorcycle, but it's not exactly clear, at least for now, just how those changes would impact performance on the circuit.
The suspension system remains the same as before as well, meaning KYB components in the form of a 48 mm coil spring fork at the front with 310 mm of travel and a shock at the rear with 305 mm of travel. Engineers did tamper with the settings of the suspension system, though, meant to improve balance and damping control.
In this revised incarnation, the motorcycle moves on aluminum wheels sized 21 inches at the front and 19 inches at the rear. They are both shod in Pirelli MX32 mid-soft tires capable of providing the proper amount of grip.
Triumph targeted other components of the two-wheeler to make it better at its job. There are, for instance, a new 50-tooth final drive, new separate stop and start switches for the rider interface, and an accessory Wi-Fi module to go with the MX Tune Pro app that offers riders a choice of ten additional engine maps.
Just like before, because this is essentially a competition machine, it comes equipped with a dashboard that is meant to supply riders with live engine data, diagnostics, and service alerts.
Finally, Triumph gave the 2027 TF 450-X a new look, going this time for a completely black appearance contrasted by yellow Triumph Racing accents.
The bike is already up and about on the bike maker's configurators, meaning it can already be ordered in this refreshed form. On the American market, the asking price starts at $10,295, making it a solid choice for those in the market for a new off-roader.

How do you know when you’re in a technological renaissance? When science, technology, and economics have lined up to produce something new.
COMMENTARY
In Europe it took artists, scientists, and craftspeople until 1550 to recognize that they had created the Renaissance—about 200 years into the revival of the classical teachings of ancient Greece and Rome, flowering of the arts and literature, and the beginnings of modern science. Today, we can see that we are in a renaissance in nuclear science and technology, and that it started only about a decade ago. We should take advantage of this realization.
The last few months have made it obvious. Since June, developers of five different reactor models have sustained “initial criticalities,” essentially very low-power chain reactions, to demonstrate the physics of their designs. So many in such quick succession is an unprecedented streak of milestones.
These are still a long way from being commercial products, but advanced reactors are under construction—in Wyoming, Idaho, and Tennessee—with construction of another due to begin in Texas. The companies behind those projects are among at least five that have each raised more than $1 billion in start-up funding.
Depending on how you count, there are a dozen start-up advanced reactor companies trading on Wall Street, and several more in related fields, like uranium enrichment. Others, seeing investor enthusiasm, have announced plans to go public.
Several states have established offices to assist nuclear companies in getting started within their borders, or set aside money to help. And the White House has set goals for nuclear expansion, as an investment in national security, among other benefits.
The politics of nuclear have changed, from New England to California. All six New England governors recently pledged to consider nuclear in their energy plans, even though several of those states passed moratoria on construction of new reactors over the last few decades. And California has reversed course to keep a nuclear power plant open because it is seen as essential to energy supply and global warming goals. The state is also hosting numerous nuclear start-ups with ambitious technical plans.
To borrow a phrase—from the medieval era, not the renaissance—the stars are lining up. When it happens in the heavens, this rare alignment is called a syzygy. Two motivating factors are external to the nuclear field: energy demand is growing and projected to grow sharply in the near future, and worldwide there is more concern about carbon-loading of the atmosphere and the oceans with greenhouse gases. Nuclear can help solve both. And two more are native to nuclear: a new generation of researchers and engineers are turning to the field, and they are using new tools, from 3D printing to artificial intelligence, to reduce costs and speed up construction.
If we recognize a pattern in these developments, how should we respond, to maximize the benefit to our prosperity, health, and security?
For starters, look ahead to the predictable bottlenecks, and move to minimize them. Tennessee and New York are funding new programs to train young people to work in the nuclear energy industry, for example. And the U.S. Department of Energy has taken a few steps to beef up the supply chain, for fuel and for critical components whose cost can be minimized if suppliers see a predictable demand. We should also improve coordination between government and industry to promote exports of nuclear energy hardware, which will help achieve economies of scale for factory-produced components, help the environment worldwide, meet the ravenous energy demand of countries with emerging economies, and improve American influence around the world.
The end point isn’t clear yet. Some of the designs now emerging will advance to commercial prototypes and then commercial production. A few will achieve commercial successes. Others, as faced by start-ups in all fields, will fall by the wayside. But this is a far cry from the 1980s, 1990s, and 2000s, when there were hardly any “new builds” in nuclear.
We can also help by recognizing that visible progress will not be smooth. Field engineers will find practical problems with designers’ work. Many of the new designs are less challenging to build, because they will operate at lower temperatures, but we will find problems with materials and fabrication techniques. And in first-of-a-kind projects, industrial mishaps are not unknown.
We should recognize that we are at a technological and commercial inflection point, even if the path ahead will not be as rosy as a Renaissance painting. It is a syzygy none the less, and we should embrace it.
— Mark Todd Peters, PhD is president of the American Nuclear Society .

By Alison Koo
5 November 2026
Congestion at several ports continues to put upward pressure on intra-Asia container freight rates, despite improving conditions at major Chinese gateways and key transhipment hubs.
The result is the Drewry Intra-Asia Container Index (IACI) is up by $46, to $1,504 per 40ft.
Spot rates from Greater China to North-east, South-east and South Asia were mostly stable during the week, as major ports, including those in China and Singapore, managed to absorb congestion.
However, smaller South-east Asian ports continued to struggle with vessel delays and operational constraints, keeping rates elevated on several tradelanes.
Rates from Shanghai to Ho Chi Minh City, Jakarta, and Laem Chabang remained high and continued to rise. At the end of October, rates from Jakarta to Shanghai were up 9% from the previous week, to $81 per 40ft.
The Shanghai Containerised Freight Index on Friday showed the Shanghai-South-east Asia rate up 2% from 30 October, to $1,164 per teu.
Jakarta’s primary port, Tanjung Priok, is struggling to cope with vessel bunching, because sudden, unscheduled multi-ship arrivals instantly overwhelm bottlenecked roads and container depots that are already at full capacity.
One forwarder at Taiwan’s Dimerco told The Loadstar Jakarta’s landside logistics had not caught up with improvements in terminal capacity.
In August, Indonesia state-owned terminal operator Pelindo preliminarily launched Terminal 2 Petikemas. However, construction of New Priok Eastern Access, a new road to improve access, only started in July, and will take 20 months to finish.
The forwarder said: “Slow turnaround makes shipping lines reluctant to absorb the costs of repositioning empty containers. This local equipment shortage drives up the prices for available containers.”
At Ho Chi Minh City, average vessel waiting times have increased from eight to 22 hours over the past fortnight, reflecting worsening congestion at the Vietnamese port. Rates from Shanghai remained unchanged, at $44 per 40ft.
In contrast, improving conditions at the major ports resulted in modest rate reductions on some routes. Rates from Shanghai to Singapore fell 3%, to $1,889 per 40ft, while those to Tanjung Pelepas declined 2%, to $2,053 per 40ft.

By Charlotte Goldstone
5 November 2026
US importers using ‘delivered duty-paid’ (DDP) shipping arrangements face increasing compliance and financial risks, as Customs and Border Protection (CBP) intensifies its scrutiny of foreign importers of record, according to CargoTrans.
Nunzio De Filippis, co-CEO, and Rennie Alston, director of trade compliance, warned that US buyers could face penalties, shipment seizures, and refused entries, even when the firm is not named as the importer of record.
During CargoTrans’s latest monthly Tariff Tea webinar, the executives said the post-Liberation Day rush towards DDP arrangements was beginning to reverse, as importers reconsidered the risks of handing control of customs formalities to overseas suppliers.
Under DDP, sellers assume responsibility for import clearance and associated duties. However, Mr Alston warned: “If you are the US consignee, if you are the US order party, if you are the instigator to the transaction, then you have culpability.”
CargoTrans said CBP was increasingly investigating whether DDP arrangements were being used to avoid tariffs, particularly where foreign sellers or intermediary platforms acted as non-resident importers of record.
Mr De Filippis said some US buyers had reported shipments being refused entry, seized, or ordered for re-export, including cases involving incorrect importer information or the use of a third-party logistics provider as the ultimate consignee.
Mr Alston warned that the consequences could extend beyond the overseas seller, with US buyers potentially facing penalties linked to their import bonds.
He suggested companies should reconsider whether DDP remained appropriate, potentially switching to ‘delivered at place’ (DAP) arrangements, to retain control of the import formalities.
For businesses continuing to use DDP, CargoTrans recommended demanding greater transparency from suppliers, including access to customs declarations, transaction documents, and supporting import data.
Mr Alston also highlighted US record-keeping requirements, warning that buyers could not simply claim ignorance of what had been declared on their behalf.
He also raised concerns about the growing volume of CBP requests for information, known as CF28s, and urged importers to investigate their records thoroughly before responding.
Mr Alston said companies should avoid rushing to meet the standard 20-day response deadline, without first checking the information internally across their procurement, finance, legal, compliance, and logistics teams. A discrepancy between supplier documentation and the original customs declaration could create additional exposure if an importer inadvertently disclosed a previously unreported compliance problem.
“Your response has to be measured,” he said.
The webinar also highlighted a shift towards CBP issuing notices of action without first requesting additional information through a CF28.
Mr Alston attributed this to greater use of customs data analytics, allowing the agency officials to make decisions using information already available through the Automated Commercial Environment (ACE) system.
Where importers disagree with a resulting assessment, they may need to pay the additional duties and subsequently challenge the decision through the ‘protest process’.
Alongside the enforcement concerns, CargoTrans highlighted several immediate tariff developments.
Revisions to the US Section 338 tariff coverage for Canadian goods took effect on 30 October, removing 22 tariff classifications from the additional 50% duty, while adding 100 others. And 178 China-related Section 301 product exclusions are scheduled to expire on 9 November, potentially thereafter exposing affected imports to additional duties, unless further action is taken.
The company also noted that a proposed extension of the suspension of China-linked vessel fees, until 9 January, had not yet been finalised.
On freight markets, CargoTrans expected selective ocean rate softening through November, particularly from North Asia and India to the US east coast. However, South-east Asian capacity remained constrained, it noted.
Finally, the company warned that rail congestion, labour uncertainty, and the planned 16-month closure of Los Angeles’ Vincent Thomas Bridge could undermine inland delivery reliability.
Its central message to importers was that cheaper ocean freight offered little benefit if customs exposure and inland disruption increased the overall cost of moving goods.

New Collaboration to Deploy Eve’s Embraer-Backed eVTOL to Southern Brazil
8 photos
Photo: Eve Air Mobility
Unlike some other eVTOL concepts that made headlines right away only to fizzle down shortly after, due to financial difficulties, the Brazilian Eve Air Mobility took things slowly and grew steadily, becoming one of the most secure and sought-after names in the emerging AAM industry worldwide.
This constant growth has a lot to do with the fact that Eve Air Mobility didn’t begin as an ambitious but inexperienced startup. Instead, it was established as the AAM (Advanced Air Mobility) subsidiary of Embraer, the Brazilian aircraft maker with a solid global reputation and a strong market presence.
That is why, although not necessarily one of the most innovative or striking eVTOL designs out there, Eve has already earned a top position among international competitors. The aircraft concept itself was further backed by a comprehensive, dedicated system of services and operational support, and this integrative approach made Eve even more appealing for operators.
One of the most recent purchase agreement will focus specifically on Southern Brazil, where the Eve eVTOL could really herald a new form of urban connectivity. This is what Gustavo Zanettini, co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of FlyBIS, believes. FlyBIS is one of the few young operators bold enough to bet exclusively on AAM as a sustainable and more efficient alternative to conventional air mobility.
FlyBIS and Eve first shook hands in 2022, and now it was time to take things to the next level through a firm order for two Eve aircraft and purchase rights for ten more units. This could mean that up to 12 eVTOLs will start operating in key areas across Southern Brazil in the near future.
Southern Brazil has two things that make it ripe for air taxi activity, namely strong tourism and intense business activity. Things aren’t set in stone, but FlyBIS predicts several air taxi routes along Santa Catarina’s coastline, with connections in cities like Navegantes and Florianopolis. Other routes could focus on tourism destinations in the mountain region of Rio Grande do Sul.
As usual with these types of agreements in an emerging sector of air mobility, the players need to handle complicated issues behind the scenes, from planning future networks and making sure that the right infrastructure is in place, to working with authorities for the safe integration of air taxi services into the wider transportation system.
So far, the full-scale prototype of the Eve eVTOL has completed 70 flights as part of an ongoing flight campaign. Transition flights will continue, as the Brazilian eVTOL reaches for the final stage of wing-borne flight. Thanks to Eve, Brazil has the potential to become one of the first countries to secure commercial-scale production for their domestic aircraft right after certification.
The Eve eVTOL has a four-passenger (plus pilot) configuration and it promises a fully electric-powered range of up to 100 km (60 miles).

SkyDrive, the AAM (Advanced Air Mobility) company that has developed what is now the most acclaimed, domestically and globally, Japanese eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing), was proud to receive an official visit from Japan’s Finance Minister, signaling an even closer focus on this new-generation aircraft and a new era of mobility.
At the end of October, a yellow eVTOL with bright red accents took to the sky and hovered over a flight test field in Yamaguchi City, Yamaguchi Prefecture. It was a SkyDrive aircraft, and the flight was a demonstration performed specifically for Japan’s Finance Minister, Satsuki Katayama.
It was a short flight of less than 10 minutes, during which the uncrewed eVTOL reached a top altitude of 30 meters (98 feet) and covered a little over 2 km (1.2 miles), flying at 78 kph (48 mph). That was enough to showcase the SD-05’s core capabilities, and Minister Katayama was particularly impressed with how quiet the electric aircraft was, and how quickly it was able to change direction.
The flight demonstration was followed by further discussions about the aircraft’s design and technology, and Minister Katayama also took a closer look at the interior of another SD-05, the one that had performed previous demonstration flights in Tokyo and at Expo 2025 Osaka.
One of the most important parts of this official visit was that representatives from SkyDrive’s official manufacturing partner were also present for talks with the Minister. That partner happens to be Suzuki Motor Corporation, which makes SkyDrive one of the very few eVTOL makers worldwide that are backed by big automotive names (the most notorious being the partnership between Archer Aviation and Stellantis for the Midnight eVTOL).
In 2024, SkyDrive announced it would start official aircraft production at a facility owned by Suzuki, and a year later, Suzuki brokered a major deal for SkyDrive in India, one of its biggest international markets, for a pre-order of up to 50 eVTOLs, from the Gujarat-based JetSetGo Aviation Services.
During this important visit, Suzuki representatives also discussed manufacturing plans with Minister Katayama, and SkyDrive representatives were confident that this event marked a step forward for their ambitious commercialization plans. Earlier this year, the Japanese Government issued a “Growth Strategy” officially confirming eVTOLs as one of the key technologies considered priorities for major investments.
SkyDrive is still in the process of securing Type Certification from the Japan Civil Aviation Bureau (JCAB), as well as eyeing future FAA (Federal Aviation Administration) certifications that will allow it to commercialize the SD-05 in the US.
This past summer, SkyDrive and FAA representatives met in Washington D.C., in the context of the 2026 FAA-EASA International Aviation Safety Conference, in preparation for kicking off the FAA certification process officially for the Japanese autonomous eVTOL.

2027 Kawasaki Ninja H2 U.S. Pricing Revealed, Supercharged Beast Goes as High as $64,300
13 photos
Photo: Kawasaki
In the first month of this fall, Japanese bike maker Kawasaki presented to the world the 2027 model year version of its flagship supercharged model, the Ninja H2. At the time, the company did not say anything about pricing on the American market. Now, as the model is about to hit American roads and tracks, that final piece of the puzzle has come to light.
In the U.S., Kawasaki launches the 2027 Ninja H2 in two versions, the Carbon ABS and the track-only derivative R ABS. They can only be ordered from November 3 to November 13, with the former going for $39,400 and the latter starting at $64,300.
As expected, those numbers are higher than they used to be for the previous model year (that would be $34,400 for the Carbon and $62,100 for the R). Kawasaki can justify the price hike, however, with the rather long and comprehensive changes it made to the Ninja.
Taking center stage is the 998cc inline-four supercharged engine that animates the two-wheeler, which, even if it's not entirely new, packs so many upgrades it could easily be considered that. Off the top of my head, there are new pistons, cylinder heads, cylinders, crankshaft, camshafts, and throttle bodies in there.
The Japanese say these upgrades, along with some others, are targeted at improving acceleration times, especially at high rpm, and greater mid-range torque. To go with all of the above, Kawasaki also throws in a lighter 4-into-1 exhaust system and an electronics package to match. Separately, Japanese engineers revised the gear ratios - it’s unclear how that translates into improved performance levels.
The frame, on the other hand, is the same as before, but it is now tied to a revised suspension system made of a KYB fork at the front and an Ohlins shock at the opposite end.
The bike employs the new Brembo Hypure brake calipers, becoming the first Kawasaki model to do so, and throws in an updated Kawasaki TRaction Control (KTRC) system with five modes and a launch control mode. The cruise control solution is new on this bike as well, as are the integrated ride modes.
Kawasaki also tampered a bit with the way the Ninja interacts with its rider, and fitted a new TFT screen that is supposedly inspired by the world of aviation. Smartphone connectivity via the Rideology app that now comes with voice commands and navigation.
Last but not least, Kawasaki throws in new heated grips and a silver mirror finish for the bodywork. That's why both the 2027 Kawasaki Ninja H2 Carbon ABS and the 2027 Kawasaki Ninja H2R ABS are available on the American market (and elsewhere) in a single color choice, something called Mirror Coated Spark Black.

YouTuber Shuts Down SEMA With 960 Cu-In 13-Rotor Quad-Turbo Miata, It's Seven Feet Tall
29 photos
Photo: Instagram/Rob Dahm (@robdahm)
Bugatti of the modern era became famous for four turbos, sixteen cylinders, 1,600 hp, and 300-mph top speed. Other carmakers settled for lesser performance numbers, but outgunned the hypercar in other ways. We won’t go into those details, because we have just come across something far more exciting than any hypercar ever made. The quadruple M - Mazda Miata Motor Mount, the SEMA 2026 build by Rob Dahm.
“Rob Dahm loves Rotary Engines. Having a wealth of knowledge in cars, and business advice, this is a one stop shop for any gear head and entrepreneur. Dahm's specialty in Lamborghini's and Mazda RX-7's make for some interesting auto adventures. Youll find a variety of Rotary Engines from 2, 3, 4, and even 6 Rotor custom creations.”
That is the YouTube description of the man’s own video outlet (spelling included). For this year’s edition of the Specialty Equipment Market Association car show, the YouTuber decided to steal the show with something far more outrageous than anything with wheels on the road (or not) today.
Of course, hypercar engineers buried countless hundreds of millions of dollars and euros into making all their powerplants actually propel the vehicle, whereas the American rotary fanatic Robert Dahm decided displacement is for those who absolutely want to have their engines work as planned.
Photo: Instagram/Rob Dahm (@robdahm) While billionaires brag about thousands upon thousands of horsepower and top speeds that would otherwise require an airplane pilot license, Dahm looked at a humble first-generation Mazda MX-5 Miata and decided that 12 Wankel rotors were too modest of an entry (and entrance) at the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas.
When electronics specialist Haltech invited him to display his diminutive single-rotor turbo roadster in Central Hall, basic common sense suggested washing the paint, which naturally meant Dahm spent 72 hours building a 13-rotor monstrosity instead. With four turbos.
Calling this contraption a 13-rotor car is reserved for the most creative of minds – the sort that conceived offshore tax havens. Rather than coupling 13 spinning triangles onto one impossible eccentric shaft, Dahm left his functional 654-cc (40-cubic-inch) turbocharged 1-rotor engine bolted in the chassis and parked his 15.7-liter (960-cubic-inch) billet-aluminum 12-rotor behemoth directly on top of it.
Photo: Instagram/Rob Dahm (@robdahm) It is the ultimate reverse-psychology parody of show cars hiding two-liter inline-fours beneath exotic covers.
Before the little Mazda could haul its overweight big brother, the bottom engine needed a surgical resurrection. Warped three-piece apex seals had tanked compression to a wheezing 60 psi (4.1 bar), dropping highway economy from 30 mpg (7.8 liters per 100 km) to 10 mpg (23.5 liters per 100 km). Dahm unpacked a fresh CNC-machined billet-aluminum rotor from New Zealand, narrowed by 0.002 inches (0.05 mm) to stop housing slap.
The rebuild blended aerospace metrology with caveman improvisation. After measuring tolerances to 0.0001 inches (0.0025 mm) and polishing the three-pinned race bearing to 0.004 inches (0.10 mm) of clearance, Dahm spent an hour sanding his old warped apex seals flat on 4,000-grit sandpaper. He then reused the old coolant rings, substituted Cosworth O-rings, slathered the housings in Valvoline VR1 20W-50 oil instead of assembly grease, and left residual dirt inside.
Photo: Instagram/Rob Dahm (@robdahm) Rob and his mechanic buddy Terry torqued the tiny block in three stages of 15 lb-ft (20 Nm), 25 lb-ft (34 Nm), and 30 lb-ft (41 Nm) before cranking the torch-heated counterweight nut to 300 lb-ft (407 Nm). Cranked with fuel disabled to build 25 psi (1.7 bar) oil pressure, the motor accidentally fired on residual fumes, idled within 10 rpm, and ripped to 9,000 rpm.
A smoothly running Miata is offensive to Dahm, so he recruited visiting German rotary fanatics to help strip his 12-rotor dragster. They removed the Circle D transmission, torque converter, manifolds, and turbos, leaving a 900-lb (408-kg) bare block dangling precariously from a 1,000-lb (454-kg) shop crane. Fabricator Ryder then welded a cradle of 1-inch steel tubing above the 1-rotor, using triangulated struts to keep the upper engine from toppling.
Quality control followed rigorous scientific protocols, meaning Dahm climbed into the engine bay and bounced his 200-lb (91-kg) frame atop the welded tubes. Satisfied that human weight basically equals a 12-rotor block, the crew transferred the aluminum monolith onto a BendPak lift and lowered it 8 inches (203 mm) above the 1-rotor. One mount bent itself into alignment while the Miata front suspension slammed onto its bump stops in agony.
Photo: Instagram/Rob Dahm (@robdahm) Seeing the two flywheels aligned vertically, Dahm briefly fantasized about gearing the 12-rotor into the 1-rotor drivetrain so it could shred the Miata transmission in two seconds flat (I think he was off by about 1.99999999 seconds). Instead, to counterbalance the front overhang and prevent snapped bolts, the crew bandsawed the bottom off the orange twin-starter housing and bolted it to the rear. Miraculously, the squashed roadster rolled by hand and drove out of the shop on 1 rotor.
To silence internet detectives at SEMA, Dahm reinstalled every functional dyno component onto the upper engine. The crew bolted on the coolant system, fuel rails, labeled wiring harnesses, three polished intake plenums, stainless headers, and three 70-lb (32-kg) Garrett turbochargers, bringing the car to four turbos including the 1-rotor below. The builder countered the crushing mass by inflating the front tires from 25 psi (1.7 bar) to 35 psi (2.4 bar).
The centerpiece of this mechanical hallucination is the center turbocharger, perched atop a stainless-steel up-pipe and Vibrant flex bellow at roof height like a gleaming rhinoceros’ horn. Fueled by pizza, brownies, and rotary sensory overload, the YouTuber took the top-heavy contraption for a midnight lap around the industrial park.
Photo: Instagram/Rob Dahm (@robdahm) His immediate complaints? The dirty windshield and the fuel filter obstructing his vision. Apparently, the skyscraper of aluminum wobbling all over the field of view was discarded from criticisms, because who doesn’t like a standing-out hood ornament? (Except the Miata doesn’t have a hood, so it’s just ornament).
Even a smoking oil line touching the lower turbo could not ruin the triumph, though loading the beast into the trailer nearly did. With about two grains’ worth of weight over the rear axle and a weight distribution of “double-everything-to-minus-zero” (don’t bring the logic pocket knife to an abstract motor naval fight, please), the Miata spun its tires and slid sideways down the first couple of feet of slick aluminum ramp.
After rotating the towering exhaust stack downward to clear the roof, Dahm charged inside, ready to traumatize every purist in Vegas. Check out the Instagram post below to see how the Miata 13-rotor quad-turbo Miata made its way to the booth.

Honda CRF1150L Africa Twin Enduro Sports Is a Tongue Twister, Weighs Less but Offers More
82 photos
Photo: Honda
I personally hate the way motorcycle makers from around the world name their products. Instead of going for straight-up names like carmakers do, they throw everything into the bike's name: their class, engine size, model family, and even the segment they play in. And that's how we end up with motorcycles named something on the line of CRF1150L Africa Twin Enduro Sports.
The name probably does not sound familiar, despite some of its component parts having been around for a while now. That's understandable, seeing how the Japanese from Honda introduced it for the first time this week at the EICMA motorcycle show in Milan, Italy.
The all-new model, as it's described, joins the bike maker's adventure offering as yet another version of the Africa Twin, really. I mean, it borrows everything of importance from that two-wheeler, including the frame, swingarm, and engine. Why, even the riding position is the same.
What the Enduro Sports brings new to the table is a lighter body (20 pounds/nine kg less than the base bike), more ground clearance, a taller seat height, and a dedicated suspension system.
Oh, and it also tampers a bit with the components it borrowed from the two-wheeler it is based on, so that all-new bike with increased off-road performance phrase Yamaha uses to describe the new model makes a lot of sense.
The Enduro Sports uses Africa Twin's steel semi-double cradle frame and its aluminum swingarm, modified to cut weight a bit, but also to better support the 1,131cc parallel twin-cylinder engine.
More ground clearance for the ride (which would be 260 mm) was achieved by using a purpose-built suspension system. It comprises 49 mm Showa closed-cartridge USD forks at the front and a shock of the same make at the rear.
Compared to the engine deployed on the other Africa Twin models, the one on the Enduro Sports is significantly more powerful, with the numbers reading 117 hp and 119 Nm of torque.
That's 16 and seven Nm more, which were gained, not in small part, on account of the powerplant being slightly larger than the version that was used until the 2026 model year (1,084cc).
The powerplant works together with a six-speed manual transmission, but there will be the option for riders to select the six-speed Dual Clutch Transmission (DCT). A redesigned intake system is on deck regardless of that choice.
The new Honda bike moves on spoked wheels sized 21 inches at the front and 18 inches at the rear, both of them shod in Metzeler Karoo Street as standard, or Michelin Anakee Wild as an option.
Honda does not say exactly when the new Africa Twin model will become available, or how much it will cost, but I can tell you for a fact that this one is not the only tongue twister in the bike maker's stable. And I will give you a single example from the refreshed range that was announced at EICMA: CRF1150L Africa Twin Adventure Sports Honda Sensing Ride.

Yamaha Previews the Future of the Tenere Adventure Bikes With Mysterious 4 Concept
12 photos
Photo: Yamaha
As I am writing this, the 2026 edition of the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show is unfolding in Milan, Italy. Everyone who's anyone in the motorcycle industry is there to show off their latest products, some more spectacular than others.
As usual, the floor of the Fiera Milano Rho is filled with present and upcoming motorcycles, but not that many concepts, because that's not how bike makers play the game. There are a few exceptions, though, and Yamaha's Tenere 4 concept draws people like a magnet.
The family of Japanese bikes that goes by the name Tenere needs little introduction. Born in the early 1980s with the XT600 Tenere, a platform derived from Yamaha's encounter with the Dakar Rally at the end of the previous decade, the lineage has grown over the years into one of the most popular ones in this segment.
The company is thus more likely to increase the number of models in the range rather than settle for what it currently has to offer. And that's exactly what the concept presented in Milan this week is here to announce.
Calling it a glimpse into the future of its expanding adventure lineup, and the result of increasing customer demand for a new lightweight machine that allows itself to be ridden by A2 license holders, Yamaha presented the Tenere 4 concept without going into all the details of its fittings and capabilities, thus ensuring mystery is ensured.
They are not hard to guess, though. An A2 bike needs to have an engine with a power rating capped at a maximum of 47 horsepower, coming from a small or medium-sized engine – and that's what will power the newcomer as well, as soon as it's ready to move from concept bike to production version.
Yamaha did share the fact that the two-wheeled concept will be fitted with adventure-ready suspension supplied by KYB on both ends, and that the fork and shock will be connected to spoked wheels sized 21 and 18 inches, respectively. As presented in Italy, the motorcycle is shod in Michelin Anakee Wild tires.
Visually speaking, the bike adopts the overall standard look of the family it is part of, but with a few particularities of its own. We've got a flat and low fuel tank, and an overall narrow profile. To one side, the bike displays a titanium Akrapovic exhaust system.
Yamaha did not say when we are to expect a bike derived from this concept to come to light. The last time the Tenere family was enriched was back in the spring of this year, when the 700 World Raid reached the United States. Later, in October, the standard and the Rally were updated here and there by Yamaha for the new, 2027 model year.

Drilling at Trilogy Metals’ Arctic project in Alaska’s Ambler mining district. Credit: Trilogy Metals.
By: Andrew Seale November 5, 2026
Alaska’s mining projects are gaining federal backing as the Trump administration seeks domestic supplies of critical minerals for national defence and the energy transition.
The U.S. Department of Defense closed a $35.6-million (C$49.3-million) investment involving Trilogy Metals (TSX, NYSE-A: TMQ) and South32 (ASX, LSE, JSE: S32) in September, giving Washington about a 10% stake in Trilogy. The proceeds are committed to advancing projects in northwestern Alaska’s undeveloped Ambler mining district.
“There is that pressure inside the administration and likely some of the pressure at those regional offices to prioritize these projects,” Finn Dobkin, senior policy analyst at George Washington University’s Regulatory Studies Center, told The Northern Miner in October.
The investment follows the reversal of federal restrictions and the addition of six Alaskan mining projects to FAST-41, a program established in 2015 to coordinate environmental reviews and authorizations for major infrastructure projects. Remote logistics, infrastructure costs and legal challenges still stand between federal support and construction.
Tuesday’s Democratic election victory adds a political caveat. The party’s capture of Congress raises the prospect of greater scrutiny of federal mining investments and could reshape permitting legislation, although reversing existing measures would generally require presidential cooperation.
Alaska hosts about 16% of the world’s defined molybdenum resources, 12% of copper resources and 7% each of gold, silver and zinc resources, according to the Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys. The division describes its comparison with global estimates as qualitative because the datasets use different criteria.
Accelerating Ambler
Trilogy’s Upper Kobuk Mineral Projects encompass about 191,000 hectares in the Ambler district and host the Arctic polymetallic deposit and Bornite copper-cobalt deposit. Ambler Metals, a joint venture owned equally by Trilogy and South32, is advancing the projects.
Development hinges on the Ambler Road, a proposed 340-km private industrial gravel road connecting the Dalton Highway with the remote district.
President Donald Trump issued a decision in October 2025 directing the Bureau of Land Management, National Park Service and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to reissue the permits needed to construct the road. It overturned a 2024 Biden administration decision and removed a major hurdle.
“We were a meme stock for about two weeks and then things settled back down to earth,” Trilogy president and CEO Tony Giardini told The Northern Miner . “We feel pretty confident in the administration defending the presidential [directive].”
The Department of the Interior transferred about 5,666 sq. km along the Dalton Highway and Trans-Alaska Pipeline corridor to the state on May 6. The transfer gives Alaska ownership and management of the land, though separate engineering and construction approvals are required for the road.
The National Parks Conservation Association and six other groups filed an appeal in Alaska Superior Court in September challenging the state’s decision to grant an easement for the industrial road.
Conservation groups and several local Indigenous communities warn it could disrupt migration of the Western Arctic caribou herd, degrade permafrost, damage salmon and shellfish habitats and threaten traditional hunting and fishing.
For Arctic, which is covered by FAST-41, the schedule targets a draft environmental impact statement in October 2027 and a federal record of decision in September 2028, Trilogy said in its third-quarter update . Ambler Metals is updating the 2023 feasibility study.
“We do expect capital to be somewhat higher,” Giardini said. “The offset is on treatment and refining charges; they’ve come down dramatically.”
The company anticipates a potential construction decision in 2028.
Donlin rising
In southwestern Alaska’s historical Kuskokwim Gold Belt, NovaGold (TSX, NYSE-A: NG) is seeking full ownership of Donlin, another project covered by FAST-41.
Donlin hosts about 560 million measured and indicated tonnes grading 2.22 grams gold per tonne for about 40 million oz., inclusive of reserves, according to a technical report effective Nov. 30, 2025. The development plan projects annual production of 1.4 million oz. in the first five years and an average of 1.1 million oz. over a 27-year mine life.
NovaGold owns 60%, with Paulson Advisers and its affiliates holding the rest. Shareholders approved the proposed all-share acquisition of Paulson’s interest at a Nov. 3 meeting, the company announced Wednesday. Completion remains targeted for the fourth quarter, subject to court, regulatory and stock exchange approvals and other closing conditions.
“It simplifies decision-making processes,” NovaGold president and CEO Greg Lang told The Northern Miner in an October interview.
The company is preparing an updated feasibility study, including capital and operating costs and a revised development schedule.
Donlin’s after-tax net present value is estimated at $5.1 billion using a gold price of $2,100 per oz. and a 5% discount rate, according to a regulatory filing from the start of the year. The previous feasibility study calculated $3 billion using $1,500 gold.
Much of the capital cost is infrastructure, including an upriver port, a connecting road, a natural gas pipeline and a power plant, Lang said.
“Donlin is a very remote site, so there’s no grid power,” he said. “We’ll need to develop an airstrip as well as a camp for both the construction workers and the mine employees.”
The company is still working on the permit for its tailings dam and water retention structures.
“A lot of geotechnical work has been done to support the permit,” Lang said. “The preliminary design packages are with the state and under review.”
Strategic minerals
Northern Dynasty Minerals’ (TSX: NDM; NYSE-A: NAK) Pebble copper-gold project, about 320 km southwest of Anchorage, remains blocked by federal restrictions protecting Bristol Bay’s salmon fishery. A federal judge heard oral arguments on June 25 in the company’s challenge to the Environmental Protection Agency’s 2023 veto, with a ruling still pending.
Pebble hosts 6.5 billion measured and indicated tonnes grading 0.40% copper and 0.34 gram gold per tonne for 57 billion lb. copper and 71 million oz. gold, plus 4.5 billion inferred tonnes at 0.25% copper and 0.25 gram gold for 25 billion lb. copper and 36 million oz. gold, according to its August 2023 assessment .
About 60 km north of Nome, Graphite One’s (TSXV: GPH; US-OTC: GPHOF) Graphite Creek project is also attracting federal support. The U.S. Geological Survey recognizes it as the country’s largest graphite deposit.
Graphite is a key material in lithium-ion batteries. The U.S. relies entirely on imports for its natural graphite supply and imported about 71,600 tonnes last year.
Graphite One received a $37.5-million Department of Defense grant in 2023 to conduct an accelerated feasibility study.
The Export-Import Bank of the United States issued non-binding letters in December indicating potential financing totalling $2.07 billion. That includes up to $670 million for Graphite Creek and $1.4 billion for an anode materials plant in Ohio.
“This is about far more than electric vehicles,” Graphite One CEO Anthony Huston told The Northern Miner . “Graphite is essential to batteries, advanced manufacturing, defence technologies and our national security.”
The federal FAST-41 schedule lists October 2027 for completion of environmental review and permitting. Graphite One targets production in 2029.
“We recognize the regulatory approvals, financing and construction milestones remain ahead of us,” Huston said. “We’re not asking for lower environmental standards; we’re asking for greater certainty, accountability and the ability to move forward responsibly.”
Returning giants
BHP (ASX, NYSE, LSE: BHP) staked new claims in Alaska and conducted aerial surveys in the southcentral region during the summer, a spokesperson told The Anchorage Press . State recorder’s office documents show dozens of claims in the Mount McKinley region.
Teck Resources’ (TSX: TECK.A, TECK.B; NYSE: TECK) project to extend the life of Red Dog, one of the world’s largest zinc mines, received FAST-41 coverage in September.
The expansion would add 14 years of production through development of the Anarraaq and Aktigiruq deposits, on state lands northwest of the existing mill.
Alaskan projects covered by FAST-41 are seeing some expedited timelines, although debate continues over the cost of moving faster, Dobkin said.
